jd:
Software Engineering Intern
We are seeking a motivated and analytical individual to join our software team. You’ll work closely with both business and technical teams to translate needs into practical solutions, support new initiatives, and test and improve what we build.


This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys problem-solving, learning how systems work, and turning ideas into action.


What You’ll Do
Understand the ask

- Work with teams across the organization to uncover what they actually need — not just what they initially ask for.
- Break large or ambiguous requirements into clear, achievable pieces of work.
- Keep the bigger picture in mind and understand how individual requests fit into the team’s overall priorities.
Learn the system

- Develop a deep working knowledge of our application: what it does, how its pieces connect, and where its edges are.
- Evaluate how new requirements interact with existing functionality.
- Identify conflicts, overlaps, dependencies, and potential downstream impacts before they become expensive problems.
Keep things moving

- Capture clear, useful notes that people can rely on weeks later.
- Coordinate meetings, make sure the right people are involved, and keep conversations moving toward decisions.
- Follow up independently and close the loop on your own work. You shouldn’t need to be reminded to chase something down.
Break things

- Test existing functionality and new features from every angle.
- Try unexpected inputs, unusual workflows, and the things users probably weren’t supposed to click.
- Perform thorough manual testing with a sharp eye for detail — both the obvious visual inconsistency and the silent data issue matter.
- Be comfortable being the person who finds the problem. That’s the point.
Write it down

- Create clear Jira stories, bug reports, feature specifications, acceptance criteria, and meeting notes.
- Write documentation that allows someone who wasn’t in the room to understand the problem and take action.
- Clearly communicate reproducible steps, expected vs. actual behaviour, and what “done” actually means.


What We’re Looking For
These qualities matter more to us than any particular technology:

- Strong communication: You can communicate clearly in writing and in conversation.
- Curiosity: You genuinely want to understand how software systems work and are willing to dig until you do.
- Organization and initiative: You manage your own threads, follow up, and close loops without being chased.
- Attention to detail: “It works” is not the end of the investigation. It’s the beginning of the next question.
- Healthy skepticism: You naturally look for edge cases, inconsistencies, and things that could go wrong.
- Comfort with ambiguity: Priorities can shift, requirements can evolve, and you’re able to adapt without losing momentum.


Our Tech Stack
You are not expected to know everything below.


We’ve intentionally grouped our stack into three tiers. Tier 1 is what we expect you to be comfortable with on day one. Tier 2 is where familiarity gives you an advantage and where you’ll grow on the job. Tier 3 is bonus territory.


Because much of this role involves understanding, evaluating, and testing software rather than building every feature end-to-end, being able to read code and reason about how it works counts. You don’t need production experience in every technology listed.


Tier 1 — Required
You should be comfortable with these fundamentals before you start:

- HTML & CSS: Layout, the box model, responsive behaviour, and understanding why something breaks at 375px.
- JavaScript: Functions, async/await, APIs, JSON, and core language fundamentals.
- React: Components, props, state, and hooks — enough to read a component and reason about what it will render.
- SQL: Basic queries, tables, joins, and relationships.
- Git: Branching, commits, pull requests, and resolving a merge conflict without panicking.
- Jira or similar: Experience is great; genuine willingness to learn it properly in your first week is required.


Tier 2 — Strongly Preferred
Familiarity is valuable; depth is a real advantage. Gaps are absolutely something you can close on the job.

- TypeScript — our front end is primarily React + TypeScript.
- Tailwind CSS — our styling layer.
- Next.js — our React framework.
- PostgreSQL — our primary database, including schema design and more complex queries.
- C# / .NET Core — our back-end services.
- Entity Framework — ORM and data-access patterns.
- Prisma — ORM on the TypeScript side.
- Database migrations — understanding what they are and why careless migrations can be dangerous.
- Wireframing & workflow mapping — Figma, Excalidraw, or even a whiteboard; you can sketch a workflow before anyone writes code.
- UI/UX sensibility — you notice when something is technically correct but frustrating to use.


Tier 3 — Bonus
Nice to have, never a barrier. We’ll teach you what you need to know.

- AWS — EC2, RDS, SQS, CloudWatch, ECR, and the wider ecosystem.
- CI/CD — understanding how code moves from a branch to production.
- AI / LLM integrations — prompt design, API integration, and evaluating model output.
- Cloud infrastructure and deployment concepts more broadly.


What You’ll Get Out of It
This is an opportunity to develop a much broader understanding of software than you’d get from simply being handed tickets.


You’ll gain:

- A real, end-to-end view of how software is specified, built, tested, and shipped.
- Direct exposure to stakeholders across the business — not just the engineering team.
- Practical experience in requirements analysis, QA, technical writing, and software delivery.
- A strong foundation for future roles in software engineering, product, business analysis, QA, or technical operations.
- Hands-on exposure to a modern full-stack environment: React/TypeScript and Next.js on the front end, .NET Core and PostgreSQL on the back end, AWS underneath it all, and AI/LLM integration work alongside it.
- Meaningful ownership of your work, with support when you need it.


If you’re the kind of person who wants to understand why something works, figure out how it fits into the bigger picture, and isn’t afraid to break things in the process, we’d love to hear from you.
fit_why: Stack fits, but role is BA/QA-heavy; C#/.NET backend gap

ABOUT US:

Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures.

WHO WE ARE:

We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy.

WHO YOU ARE:

Astro Mechanica is seeking an intern to join our Software Engineering Team for the summer of 2027 (program begins on June 7, 2027 for semester schools and June 27, 2027 for quarter schools). This is not a sandbox internship. You’ll be embedded with the team in our San Francisco office, working on real projects that ship and contribute directly to our hardware and flight programs. The ideal candidate is curious, learns quickly, and is excited to write software that touches real aircraft systems. You’ll work alongside full-time engineers, take part in design discussions and code reviews, and own meaningful pieces of work from start to finish. Your work will move fast in a dynamic startup environment and will have a direct impact on our mission.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:



- Work as an embedded member of the software team, joining standups, design reviews, and planning alongside full-time engineers
- Own a scoped, real-world project from design through implementation, testing, and delivery, with mentorship from senior engineers
- Contribute to flight software, simulation, test infrastructure, or internal engineering tools
- Test your code on real flight hardware (flight computers, embedded microprocessors, engine hardware)
- Write clean, testable, and maintainable code, including unit and integration tests
- Collaborate with mechanical, electrical, propulsion, and controls engineers to understand software requirements
- Debug issues across the stack and learn how software integrates with embedded and real-time systems
- Present your work to the team at the end of the summer

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:



- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, Math, or a Science discipline
- Experience with C++, Rust, Python, or another programming language, through coursework, projects, research, or prior internships
- Solid fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and object oriented programming
- Familiarity with version control (Git) and software testing practices
- Ambition to work in a fast-paced environment and take ownership of your work
- Available for a full-time, in-person internship in San Francisco during Summer 2027 (approximately 10–12 weeks)

PERKS & BENEFITS:



- Competitive hourly pay
- Hands-on mentorship from experienced engineers
- Company-funded perks, including team lunches, game nights, and other activities 

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

At Astro Mechanica, we highly value in-office work to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. We consider working in the office five days a week an essential part of the employee's role.

Astro Mechanica is an equal opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.
fit_why: Flight software, embedded hardware testing; candidate lacks embedded/firmware experience

Company Information

PACCAR is a global technology leader in the design, manufacture and customer support of high-quality light-, medium- and heavy-duty trucks under the Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF nameplates. PACCAR also designs and manufactures advanced power trains, provides financial services and information technology, and distributes truck parts related to its principal business.

Peterbilt Motors Company

On highways, construction sites, city streets, logging roads - everywhere our customers earn their living - Peterbilt's red oval is a familiar symbol of performance, reliability and pride. Peterbilt has reigned as America's premium quality truck manufacturer since the company's founding in 1939. Our dedication to deliver products and services focused on improving customers' performance, image, profitability and peace of mind truly makes Peterbilt the Class of the Industry.

Requisition Summary

Peterbilt Motors Company, a PACCAR Company, has an internship for students currently enrolled in college. This opening is for a Truck Systems & Software Support Intern to add to our Resident Engineering team in Denton, Texas.

Job Responsibilities

This position will be working on various projects and reports to include but not limited to:



- Shadow and assist team members in monitoring, maintaining, and troubleshooting truck fleet management systems and software platforms.
- Gather and consolidate operational data from various truck systems, databases, and reports for analysis.
- Perform data analysis to identify trends, inefficiencies, and opportunities for process improvement.
- Assist in creating spreadsheets, dashboards, and automated reporting tools to streamline team workflows.
- Evaluate current team processes and recommend data-driven solutions to enhance productivity.
- Help document software features, troubleshooting procedures, and best practices used by the Truck Systems & Software Support team.
- Work with other departments to understand how truck systems impact broader business operations.
- Support the team with special projects and assignments as assigned by management.

Required Qualifications

The candidate we seek will be currently enrolled in an Electrical, Mechanical, Computer Engineering or a related program.

Preferred Qualifications

The skills that are important to be successful in this position are as follows:



- Exceptional Microsoft Office
- Excellent verbal and written communication
- Multi-tasking
- Self-starter and Resourceful
- Strong Professionalism
- Analytical
- Interest in collecting, analyzing, and reporting on tests

General Description Of Internship Benefits

As a U.S. PACCAR intern, you have a full range of benefit options including:



- Competitive salary and 401k with up to a 5% company match
- Medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your family 
- Paid holidays
- Flexible spending accounts (FSA) and health savings account (HSA) 
- Life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance 
- EAP services including wellness plans, estate planning, financial counseling and more 
- Global Fortune 500 company with a wide array of growth, training, and development opportunities 
- Work alongside experienced goal-oriented colleagues recognized as experts in their field
- This position may offer stipend assistance benefits

Additional Job Board Information

PACCAR is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veteran/Disability corporation. Peterbilt promotes Diversity and Inclusion through mentorship, events, and affinity support groups – The Diversity Council, Peterbilt Women’s Initiative (PBWIN), Veterans Group, Peterbilt Black Organization for Leadership and Development (B.O.L.D) and Peterbilt+ (An LGBTQ support group).
fit_why: Requires enrollment in Electrical/Mechanical/Computer Engineering; truck fleet systems focus

Spring 2027 Internship: This position is located at our Frisco, TX office. Expected program dates are January 19 – April 23, 2027. Anticipated working hours will be 20-30 per week, 2-3 days a week on-site.

Note: Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions will not be providing visa sponsorship for this position now or in the future. Therefore, in order to be considered for this position, you must have the ability to work without a need for current or future visa sponsorship.

Introduction

The Agentic Software Engineering Intern contributes within the software development team to learn and aid with development, test, and support of Toshiba’s Point of Sale (POS) solutions in the retail marketplace, collaborating within the agile development team in a fast-paced, customer-first environment. These solutions include point of sale (POS), customer loyalty solutions, and mobile applications (Android, iOS). Many technologies are used, including SaaS (Software as a Service), SOA (Service Oriented Architecture), MoM (Message Oriented Middleware), cloud computing, enterprise, and desktop Java development.

Must Have



- This is an in-person role at least 2-3 days a week in person.
- Familiarity with LLM integration (e.g., calling APIs, using Hugging Face or LangChain frameworks).
- Agentic System Knowledge (Prompt Engineering, LLM, RAG, Vector Databases)

Responsibilities



- Assist engineers in a subset of the following areas as assigned: 

- Programming duties include coding, design, testing, system maintenance, building defined features, investigation/troubleshooting, and fixing/verifying defects 
- Resolution of technical challenges requiring a narrow scope of domain and discipline knowledge 
- Implementation of product and solution features, according to guidance; solutions involve enterprise-, cloud- and client-side components which may leverage Java, JavaScript, and modern UI frameworks, RESTful microservices with JSON & Swagger, and relational and no-SQL databases 
- Participate in the design, development, implementation, testing, and maintenance of systems supporting a variety of applications and business-critical functionality. 
- Work directly within the agile development team and stakeholders to help with existing requirements, adhere to timelines, and meet deliverables. 
- Learn about TGCS product offerings and how clients use them. 
- Learn about how TGCS products go from an idea to a fully-fledged product. 
Required Skills



- Currently pursuing Computer Science/Engineering major in Undergraduate Studies
- Excellent analytical skills 
- Ability to work in a fast paced, team-based environment 
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills 
- Programming and analytical skills, problem determination and debugging, attention to detail, teamwork and excellent communication skills. 
- Effective verbal and written communication; able to read, write, and speak English proficiently   

Preferred Skills



- Participation in agile SDLC; usage of agile project management tools  
- Ability to use code versioning tools like Git, SVN, etc. 
- Software development experience with Java, C++, or similar 
- Modern web development experience, including application of HTML5, JavaScript, CSS, and various JS frameworks such as Angular, React, or Vue.JS.

jd:
Venture outside the ordinary - TMX Careers

The TMX group of companies includes leading global exchanges such as the Toronto Stock Exchange, Montreal Exchange, and numerous innovative organizations enhancing capital markets. United as a global team, we’re connecting cross-functionally, traversing industries and geographies, moving opportunity into action, advancing global economic growth, and propelling progress. Through a rich exchange of ideas, meaningful collaboration, and a nimble operating model, we're powering some of the nation's most critical systems, fueling capital formation and innovation, bringing increased opportunity to business visionaries, product ingenuity to consumers, and career exploration to our team.

Ready to be part of the action?

As generative AI tools rapidly enter the workplace, how do employees know which tools are safe, vetted, and approved to use? The AI Governance & Policy intern will help answer this question by bridging policy, technology, and user accessibility. Reporting into the AI Operations & Responsible AI team, you will take direct ownership of modernizing and managing our Approved AI Registry—transforming a growing internal inventory of tools and models into a searchable, intuitive, and user-friendly knowledge resource. You will also support the research, drafting, and plain-language editing of evolving Responsible AI standards and internal guidelines. This role is ideal for an analytical, curious student from the humanities, public policy, political science, communications, or legal studies who loves synthesizing complex information into clear, human-centered content.



- This role reports to: Technology Partner, AI Operations & Responsible AI
-  Chief Client Delivery Officer
- Job Location: Hybrid (2-3 days in office) - based in Toronto, ON. 

Key Accountabilities



- Approved AI Registry & Knowledge Hub: Take day-to-day ownership of maintaining our central registry of approved AI tools, services, and models. Restructure, categorize, and redesign the list so employees across the company can quickly search, understand allowed use cases, and identify restrictions. 
- Intranet & Content Accessibility: Build and maintain an intuitive internal intranet portal/wiki (e.g., SharePoint, Confluence) where staff can easily navigate AI policies, FAQs, templates, and guidance documents. 
- Inventory Integration: Partner across teams (AI & Data, Legal, ERM) as we build out our enterprise AI and model inventory, ensuring data connections between approved vendor tools and internal systems remain accurate and up to date. 
- Policy Research & Plain-Language Editing: Review, polish, and help draft internal AI guidelines, standards, and committee briefing materials. Translate dense technical configurations and legal/regulatory nuances into clear, engaging, and accessible guidance. 
- Special Projects & Emerging Technology Tracking: Conduct desktop research on emerging AI standards, regulatory developments, and industry best practices to support upcoming governance initiatives. 

Must Have(s)



- Currently enrolled in an accredited undergraduate or graduate co-op program in Public Policy, Political Science, Legal Studies, Communications, Philosophy, English, History, Information Management, or an interdisciplinary technology/society program. 
- A clear interest in artificial intelligence, including personal engagement with current challenges, ethical questions, or policy implications surrounding AI adoption. 
- Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex, technical, or legal subject matter and translate it into clear, plain-language documentation. 
- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with strong attention to detail. 
- Strong organizational skills and information architecture aptitude (e.g., structuring messy data/spreadsheets, categorizing inventories, or organizing intuitive documentation). 
- High degree of intellectual curiosity for emerging technologies and an ownership mindset when tackling ambiguous challenges. 

Nice to Have(s)



- A public GitHub repository or digital portfolio showcasing writing, research, policy briefs, or information management projects. 
- Familiarity with enterprise collaboration and knowledge management tools (e.g., SharePoint, Confluence). 

Notes:



- 4 month Co-op Internship: January 11, 2027 to April 30, 2027
- In order to be considered for the position, you are required to submit your Knockri Assessment

Salary Range: $20.00/hour - $23.00/hour CAD. Please note that the salary range included is a guideline only. The salary offered may vary based on factors, including, but not limited to, the successful candidate’s relevant knowledge, skills, and experience.

The recruiting efforts for this role are intended to fill a vacant position.

For this role AI-assisted tools are utilised as one input in the application and screening process. AI does not make final hiring or interview decisions.

In the market for…

Excitement - Explore emerging technology and innovation, as well as ventures and digital finance that shape the future of global markets! Experience the movement of the market while grounded in the stability of close to 200 years of success.

Connection - With site hubs in some of the world’s most multicultural cities, we leverage our size and structure to create rich connections and belonging while experiencing powerful global impact through our work.

Impact - More than a platform, we use our talents to power mission-critical systems that drive global economic advancement, innovation, and growth. As well, our employee-led Team Impact spreads social good via our giving strategy.

Wellness - From empathetic leadership to a culture of flexibility and balance, we believe wellness at work creates the maximum yield and a stronger “we”. Plus, with a cloud-first and hybrid workstyle, as well as generous time-off and leaves, we support a life well lived!

Growth - From a growth mindset in our work, to expansion in our business, TMX is home to action-takers energized by the achievement of ambitious growth.

Ready to enrich your career with impactful work, leaders who truly care, and the flexibility and programs to help you thrive as part of #TeamTMX ? Apply now.

Please note that our company is not currently sponsoring work permit applications and the applicant must be authorized to work in the country where this position is located. 

TMX is committed to creating and sustaining a collegial work environment in which all individuals are treated with dignity and respect and one which reflects the diversity of the community in which we operate. We provide accommodations for applicants and employees who require it.
